concept.title: Cross-References and Hyperlinks
concept.abstract: This section covers Cross-References, Bookmarks and Hyperlinks — three distinct navigational mechanisms that connect related content within a document, across a documentation set, or to an external resource — and six scenarios: an internal cross-reference or bookmark, an external URL, a hyperlink with non-descriptive display text, a link list at the end of a section, and an internal link list used as a mini-TOC. The converter maps each structured link to a DITA <xref> element using @href, @scope, and @format to resolve the target correctly in the generated output

conbody.p: A cross-reference, a bookmark, and a hyperlinkare three distinct mechanisms - each with a specific structural role:

ul.li: A cross-reference is an active, field-based link to a heading, figure, table, footnote, or bookmark within the same document or internal identifier (such as bookmark).

A bookmarkassigns a named identifier to a specific location in the document — a word, a phrase, a paragraph, or a position between characters. Bookmarks serve as anchor points that cross-references and hyperlinks can target.Both cross-reference and/or bookmarks target updates automatically when the document is restructured or the sections are moved within the same document.

A hyperlinkstores an explicit address — a URL, an email address, a file path, or a sometimes same-document bookmark anchor. Unlike bookmark and cross reference, the hyperlink address is fixed at the time of creation.Using the document's native link tools is the condition that produces a valid, resolvable element in the DITA output. A link typed as plain text produces no link structure and maps to a plain

element.

conbody.p: In HTML, links are created using the <a> element with an href attribute that identifies the target location. The converter evaluates the target of each HTML <a> element when generating DITA output and resolves each link type using three <xref> attributes:

row.entry: Topic file path, URL, mailto: address
local — same deliverable peer — same documentation set, different deliverable external — outside the documentation set
Cross-reference - dita — default for DITA topic references Hyperlink - html — external web pages; PDF — linked PDF files

conbody.note: Ensure all hyperlinks reference valid targets and use descriptive link text. The converter flags unresolvable links in the conversion report.
